## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (ollaya-f32, needs 4.6 GB, NVIDIA only, from [github.com/ollaya-dev](https://github.com/ollaya-dev/ollaya/blob/9b8698e39f11a0f0bcd08ad686de51cd1b4f6fa8/results/runs/2026-10-14-latency-rtx5090-cuda.json))
   
   ```sh
   ollaya run kev:0.8b --preset triage "The customer requests a refund."
   ```

[Download model files](https://huggingface.co/jaredpalmer/kev-0.8b/tree/bf75a6a8848ea6960ff2ed108d9ed44c2941174f) · Published model files verified. Includes adapters or readout weights; follow the model documentation for the required base model. This is a verified repository snapshot; the benchmark does not establish an identical weight revision. A matching Ollaya runtime manifest and published short-workload GPU memory measurement were reviewed separately; see local variants and identity\_note. The command was not executed in this review. [Evidence](https://huggingface.co/api/models/jaredpalmer/kev-0.8b/revision/bf75a6a8848ea6960ff2ed108d9ed44c2941174f); checked 2026-10-31.
